explanation: Formal meetings, especially with government officials, senior executives, or foreign partners, call for punctuality in Indonesia, while a more relaxed attitude toward time — often nicknamed 'jam karet' (rubber time) — is common in informal or social settings. Hierarchy also matters: being late to meet someone senior is viewed less favorably than minor lateness among peers. It's safest to aim for on-time arrival and give notice if delayed.
local_tip: Arrive on time for formal or government meetings, and if you're running late, send a brief message ahead rather than showing up without warning.

also_check.note: Punctuality is strictly observed; arriving late is a serious breach of etiquette.
Punctuality is highly valued; lateness is seen as disrespectful.
Lateness of 15-30 minutes is common socially but less acceptable for formal business meetings.
